We break up the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We start by calculating the second of these integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{36x}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let $u=2+3{x}^{2}$,  then $\text{d}u=6x\,\text{d}x.$ Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{36x}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{6}{{u}^{3}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{3}{{u}^{2}}+C \\  & =-\frac{3}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{2}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{36x}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}\frac{36x}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }({-\frac{3}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{2}}|}_{0}^{a}\,) \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }(-\frac{3}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{2}}+\frac{3}{(2+0)^{2}}) \\  & =-0+\frac{3}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand $\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}$ is an **even** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that 

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{36|x|}{{(2+3{x}^{2})}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{4}+\frac{3}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
